query: Consider the following context: Temper embrittlement, characterized by a dramatic loss of ductility within a narrow temperature window, is ubiquitous in conventional alloys but is not reported in compositionally complex or high‐entropy alloy systems. In that context, which material can be used for ductile–brittle–ductile transition, and why?

generation.hypothesis: The ductile–brittle–ductile transition in high-entropy alloys can be achieved by optimizing the alloy composition, specifically by adjusting the content of elements such as Cr, which can form brittle intermetallic compounds, and by controlling the processing temperature and phase composition.
generation.material_initial_state: High-entropy alloy with varying compositions (e.g., CoCrFeMnNi, AlCoCrFeNi)
generation.intervention: Adjusting the content of elements such as Cr and controlling the processing temperature and phase composition
generation.structural_mediator: Formation of brittle intermetallic compounds and secondary phases
generation.mechanism: Optimization of alloy composition and processing conditions to minimize the formation of brittle phases
generation.predicted_outcome: Improved ductility and reduced brittleness in high-entropy alloys
generation.baseline: Conventional high-entropy alloys with limited ductility
generation.boundary: Temperature and composition ranges that induce brittle behavior
generation.uncertainty: The exact relationship between alloy composition, processing conditions, and ductile–brittle–ductile transition is not fully understood and requires further investigation

falsification_experiment.design: Systematic variation of alloy composition and processing conditions to measure the resulting ductility and brittleness
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If the optimized alloy composition and processing conditions do not result in improved ductility and reduced brittleness, the hypothesis is falsified

cited_evidence.text: Gap and lever. Type: tradeoff. Statement: The paper notes that while adding Cr improves oxidation resistance, it promotes the precipitation of Laves phase which can be brittle, though the authors do not explicitly quantify a ductility loss in this specific study.. System: WVTaTiCr x refractory high-entropy alloy. Lever: Cr content. Quote: "Unfortunately, elements Al, Cr, and Si very easily form brittle intermetallic compounds with other refractory elements, resulting in reduced mechanical properties of RHEAs"

Gap and lever. Type: limitation. Statement: The authors report that the alloy exhibits brittle behavior at room temperature, limiting its immediate application in scenarios requiring ductility.. System: CoCrFeNiTi high-entropy alloy. Lever: processing temperature or phase composition. Quote: "Compression testing revealed that the SPS–processed AlCrFeTiX (X = Co, Ni, Cu) alloys exhibited brittle behavior at room temperature (25 °C)."

Gap and lever. Type: future_work. Statement: Future work is needed to verify the crack-free processing capability of newer alloy compositions that promise increased ductility.. System: Al 10 Nb 15 Ta 5 Ti 30 Zr 40. Lever: alloy composition. Quote: "More recently developed refractory metal high entropy alloys like Al 10 Nb 15 Ta 5 Ti 30 Zr 40 [ [49] ] promise an increased room temperature ductility and hence crack-free processing by PBF-LB/M even without high temperature build-platform heating, which needs to verified in future work"
